items.title: 李대통령 국정평가 긍정 40%-부정 49%
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령 국정수행에 대한 긍정 평가가 40%, 부정 평가가 49%로 집계됐다. 한국갤럽이 17∼19일 전국 유권자 1001명을 대상으로 실시해 20일 발표한 여론조사(전화면접 방식·95% 신뢰수준에 표본오차 ±3.1%포인트·자세한 사항은 중앙선거여론조사심의위원회 홈페이지 참조)에 따르면 이 대통령이 “잘하고 있다”는 답변은 40%, “잘못하고 있다”는 답변은 49%였다. 지난주 조사에선 각각 39%, 50%였다. 긍정 평가 이유로는 외교(24%)와 경제·민생(12%) 등이 많았고 부정 평가 이유로는 경제·민생(18%), 도덕성 문제·본인 재판 회피(13%), 부동산 정책(12%) 등을 많이 꼽았다. ‘향후 1년간 우리나라 경제가 좋아질 것’이라는 낙관 전망은 26%, ‘나빠질 것’이란 비관 전망은 38%였다. 경기 낙관론은 올 6월까지...

items.snippet: ▲ 11월 7일 자 A12면 ‘결혼 6년 만에 낳은 아이, 최고의 피로회복제’ 기사에서 ‘여성가족부’는 ‘성평등가족부’의 잘못이므로 바로잡습니다. ▲ 9일 자 B1면 ‘독일車가 어쩌다가… BMW “올해 이익률 -0.5~0.5%”’ 기사의 그래픽에서 메르세데스-벤츠그룹의 2026년 3분기 영업이익 ’5600만유로’를 ‘5억6000만유로’로 바로잡습니다.

items.title: 법조계 “與, 정상적인 절차 빌려 헌법 파괴”
items.snippet: 지난 19일 대법원이 한덕수 전 국무총리 내란 사건을 일부 무죄 취지로 파기환송한 뒤, 더불어민주당이 조희대 대법원장 탄핵을 추진하는 데 대해 법조계에서는 “심각한 삼권분립 침해”라는 지적이 나왔다.

items.title: SKY 의대 합격선 ’298점‘… 작년보다 최고 10점 올라
items.snippet: 지난 19일 치러진 2027학년도 수능 가채점 결과, 올해 서울 주요 대학 의대 합격선이 작년보다 4~10점 오를 것으로 예측됐다. ‘킬러 문항’(초고난도 문항)이 없었고, 국어와 영어 영역이 작년보다 쉽게 출제된 영향이라는 게 입시 전문가들의 분석이다.

items.title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force
items.snippet: New rules on what Airbnb hosts can reasonably ask guests to do could mean fewer chores but higher costs for customers.

items.title: 수원 화성에 뜬 ‘조선 제일검’
items.snippet: 20일 경기 수원시 화성행궁 앞에서 수원시립공연단이 전통 무예 공연을 하고 있다. 갑옷을 입은 단원이 칼로 짚단을 베고 있다.

items.title: SM 주가 조작 혐의 김범수, 2심도 무죄
items.snippet: 서울고법 형사4-1부(재판장 김인겸)는 20일 SM엔터테인먼트(SM) 인수 과정에서 주가를 조작한 혐의(자본시장법 위반 등)로 기소된 김범수 카카오 창업자에게 무죄를 선고했다. 1심에 이어 항소심에서도 무죄가 선고돼 김 창업자는 사법리스크를 상당 부분 벗게 됐다.

items.title: 위례 비리 등 3차례 조사에도 수사·기소 위법성 발견 안돼
items.snippet: 과거 검찰이 수사권을 남용했는지 조사하겠다며 출범한 검찰인권존중미래위원회(검찰미래위)는 20일 진상조사단에게 위례 신도시 개발 비리, 문재인 정부 부동산 통계 조작 사건과 관련한 보완조사 결과를 다시 보고받았다. 지난달 15일, 이달 5일에 이어 세 번째 보고다. 진상조사단은 두 차례 추가 보완조사에도 여전히 “검찰 수사에서 위법성을 발견하지 못했다”고 보고했는데도, 검찰미래위는 결론을 내지 않고 있다.

items.title: “지방서 일할 의사 모십니다” 일당 100만원 주고, 은퇴한 70대 채용
items.snippet: 충북 충주시는 이달 초 70대 초반의 퇴직 전문의를 기간제 의사로 채용했다. 지역 내 공중보건의사(공보의)가 줄자, 기간제 의사를 보건지소(읍·면 단위 공공의료기관) 순회 진료에 투입하기로 했다. 과거 13명이던 의과 공보의가 지금은 2명만 남아 있고, 이들마저 내년 4월 복무를 마치면 한 명도 남지 않기 때문이다. 시 관계자는 “기간제 관리 의사 추가 채용도 검토 중”이라고 했다.

items.title: 중증 감염병인데… 항생제 투여 하루만에 등교를?
items.snippet: 일선 학교에 배포된 감염병 예방·위기 대응 매뉴얼이 오히려 현장에 혼란을 주고 있다. 중증 감염병에 걸린 학생에게 항생제 치료 하루 만에 등교를 해도 되는 것처럼 나와 있거나, 감염 여부를 제대로 알 수 없는 시점을 ‘등교 중지 기간’으로 정하는 등 이를 그대로 적용하기 어렵다는 지적이 나온다. 바로 교육부와 질병관리청 등이 2023년 12월 만든 학교 감염병 대응 매뉴얼이다.

items.title: [알립니다] 치매 진단·치료법 알려드려요
items.snippet: 삼성서울병원과 조선일보사가 마련하는 ‘랜선 건강교실’ 11월 영상이 업로드됐습니다. 이번 건강교실 주제는 ‘치매’입니다. 현대 사회에서 가장 두려운 뇌 질환으로 꼽히는 치매에 관한 진단과 치료 방법 등 다양한 궁금증을 삼성서울병원 신경과 김희진 교수가 자세히 풀어드립니다.

items.title: 주말까지 춥다… 체감 영하 10도
items.snippet: 절기상 소설(小雪)인 22일 아침까지 영하권 추위가 이어지겠다. 바람도 강하게 불면서 중부 내륙에선 체감온도가 영하 10도 안팎까지 내려갈 것으로 예상된다. 호남과 제주에는 21일까지 눈이 내리겠다.

items.title: 화재 현장서 외국인 16명 대피 도운 박진용씨 ‘용감한 의인’ 서울시 표창
items.snippet: 서울시 소방재난본부는 지난 1일 관악구 숙소 화재 현장에서 외국인 투숙객 16명을 대피시킨 회사원 박진용(37)씨에게 ‘재난 현장 용감한 의인’ 표창을 수여했다고 20일 밝혔다. 당시 오토바이를 타고 지나가던 박씨는 숙소에서 불길이 치솟자 곧바로 119에 신고했다. 오후 2시 18분쯤이었다. 이어 불이 난 3층으로 올라가 객실 문을 두드리며 “불이야”라고 외쳤다. 스페인 단체 관광객 12명 등 외국인 투숙객 16명은 그제야 불이 난 사실을 알고 대피했다. 불은 2시간여 만에 꺼졌고 인명 피해는 없었다. 서울시는 “박씨가 위험한 상황에서도 용기 있는 행동을 했다”고 했다. 박씨는 “연기가 많이 나서 안에 있는 사람들에게 알리려고 올라갔다”며 “당연한 일을 했을 뿐”이라고 했다.

items.title: “한류, 잠깐의 유행 아닌 학문으로 남길 겁니다”
items.snippet: 영국 옥스퍼드대의 유서 깊은 회의장 ‘콘보케이션 하우스’에 판소리 가락이 울려 퍼졌다. 900년 넘는 이 대학 역사상 처음으로 ‘한국학센터(The Oxford Centre for Korean Studies)’가 지난 19일 문을 열었다. 초대 소장을 맡은 조지은(50) 교수는 “처음 영국에 온 25년 전엔 상상도 못한 장면이라 가슴이 벅찼다”고 했다. 석·박사까지 배출할 수 있는 한국학센터 출범으로 옥스퍼드대 내 한국학 강의가 대폭 늘고 다양해질 전망이다.

items.title: 엄마가 그리운 날엔 ‘엄마 어렸을 적엔’ 이야기 속으로…
items.snippet: 지금으로부터 30년 전, 많은 국민의 공감을 불러일으킨 못난이 인형들이 있었다. 1960~1970년대 순박하고도 정이 넘쳤던 우리 부모 세대의 자화상을 닮은 이 못난이 인형들을 들여다보며 어떤 이는 눈물짓기도, “그땐 그랬지~” 하며 고개를 끄덕이기도 했다. 1996년 조선일보미술관 전시를 비롯해 예술의전당, 지방 전시장을 순회하며 180만 관람객을 불러 모았던 이승은·허헌선 부부의 인형전 ‘엄마 어렸을 적엔…’ 얘기. 당시 전시를 통해 ‘데뷔’한 못난이 인형들은 이후 초·중·고 교과서에도 실릴 만큼 화제가 되며 ‘국민 인형’ 못지않은 인기를 누리기도 했다.

items.title: 뒤집어 알고 있던 것들
items.snippet: 왼쪽 아래 송곳니가 길고 날카롭다는 느낌에 한동안 불편했다. 입을 다물 때마다 아래 송곳니가 윗니와 먼저 닿는 느낌이었다. 대개 몸의 어떤 부위가 의식되고 신경 쓰인다는 건 그 자리에 문제가 있다는 신호다. 의식하면 더 나빠진다. 캐스터네츠처럼 윗니와 아랫니를 딱딱 치는 습관이 생겼다. 치과에서 엑스레이를 찍어보니 이 습관이 문제였다. 씹는 힘을 지속적으로 받는 송곳니 끄트머리가 마모되고 떨어져 나가 손상되지 않은 부위, 온전한 치아가 길고 날카롭게 느껴졌던 것이었다. 의사가 엑스레이 화면에 치아가 떨어져 나간 자리를 그려 설명해줬다. 솟은 자리가 아니라 떨어져 나간 자리였다니, 뒤집어 알고 있었다.

items.title: 스메타나, 드보르자크가 낳은 ‘프라하의 봄’
items.snippet: 바츨라프 광장 끝 국립박물관 1층 중앙홀엔 체코를 대표하는 54점의 동상, 흉상을 전시하는 판테온이 있다. 종교 개혁의 선구자로 나섰다 화형당한 얀 후스와 함께 스메타나, 드보르자크같은 음악가가 포함돼있다. 체코인의 정체성과 단결을 고취하는 민족주의 상징으로 음악가를 내세운 것이다.

items.title: 소음에 귀 기울이지 말라 [안광복의 주말의 철학]
items.snippet: 로마 장군 파비우스 막시무스의 별명은 ‘굼뜬 사람(cunctator)’이었다. 한니발이라는 무시무시한 적장에 맞선 그의 군대는 좀처럼 싸우려 나서지 않았다. 보급선을 위협하며 소소한 싸움만 걸었을 뿐이다. 조급해진 로마 시민들의 비난이 빗발쳤다. 그래도 파비우스는 묵묵히 끈질기게 한니발의 뒤를 따라다니기만 했다. 마침내, 전쟁이 끝났을 때 ‘굼뜬 사람’이라는 별명은 최고의 영예가 됐다. 만약 막강했던 한니발의 군대와 크게 한판 붙었으면 로마의 군단은 결딴났을 터다. 파비우스가 충분히 시간을 끌어주었기에, 로마는 그에게 맞설 만큼 힘을 기를 수 있었다.

items.title: 한국의 의료계가 ‘성역’이라고?
items.snippet: 올 하반기 소아청소년과 전공의 모집 정원이 119명인데, 2명 지원했다. 이대로 가면 소아청소년과 의사의 씨가 마를 판이었다. 그런데 엎친 데 덮친 격이라고 그 와중에 아주대 소아응급실 압수수색 사태까지 터졌다. 이제 다음 번 전공의 모집 때는 지원자가 아예 제로로 떨어지는 것은 아닐까? 그야말로 소아청소년 진료라고 하는 우리 의료의 한 분야 자체가 붕괴될 지경이다. 그런데, 놀랍게도 우리 사회 일각에서는 볼멘소리도 나오는 것 같다. ‘의사가 성역이냐?’는 것이다. ‘의사도 국민인데, 범죄신고가 들어오면 압수수색도 받고 진료하다 환자가 죽으면 형사처벌을 받는 것이 당연하지 않느냐’는 것이다.

items.title: 나이 듦이 가져다주는 선물 [고혜련의 삶이 있는 풍경] (29)
items.snippet: 겨울을 향해 손짓하며 찬연한 오색 단풍과 낙엽이 천지를 물들이는 늦가을. 사계절이 있는 이 강토가 새삼 고맙다. 사계절은 마치 인간들에게 주어진 생명의 변화를 잘 살피도록 짜인 각본 같다. 천지를 찬란하게 물들이며 아름다움을 뽐내는 늦가을을 그냥 보내는 게 ‘예의가 아닌 듯해’ 단풍이 절정인 곳을 찾아 나섰다. 단풍의 황홀함에 대한 뻔한 찬사 같지만 아니다. 자연에 빠져 인생 행로조차 바꾼 사람에게 대자연을 칭하는 ‘마더 네이처(Mother Nature)’가 만물의 위대한 어머니, 조물주의 사랑으로 다가오는 것에 응답하기 위해서다. 이파리를 모조리 떨궈 자신의 온몸을 흙으로 내려놓는 나무의 자태가 절묘하고 숭고한 섭리로 보인다. 일견 “이제 준비하라”는 귀띔 같다. 나이가 들긴 들었나 보다. 나이 듦이 가져다주는 선물은 감사한 마음이 보다 자...

items.title: 실용적이고 눈에 띄어… 비녀 사러 갑니다
items.snippet: 16일 낮 1시쯤 서울 종로구 동대문종합시장 액세서리상가. 한 외국인이 나비 장식이 달린 옥색 비녀를 집어 들었다. 그러고는 같은 제품 여섯 개를 결제했다. 미국인 관광객 세라(50)씨는 “한국적인 디자인이 많아 고급스러워 보이는 데다 실용적”이라며 “선물용으로 여러 개 산 것”이라고 했다. 한복을 입을 때 주로 쓰던 전통 장신구인 비녀를 찾는 이들이 늘고 있다. 비녀가 평상복에도 어울리는 머리 장식으로 자리 잡고 있는 것이다. 외국인 관광객 사이에서는 한복 체험 때 잠시 꽂는 소품을 넘어 일상에서 쓸 수 있는 ‘한국식 패션 아이템’으로 인기를 끈다. 머리를 간단히 틀어 올려 고정할 수 있는 데다 하나만 꽂아도 눈에 띄는 장식이 된다는 점이 인기 요인으로 꼽힌다.

items.title: 인생서 독일 만난 건 행운... 통일·복지정책 많이 배웠다
items.snippet: 이미륵상은 한독협회와 독한협회가 1999년 이미륵 박사 탄생 100주년을 기념해 제정한 상입니다. 이미륵 박사는 1899년 황해도 해주에서 태어나 서울에서 의학 공부를 하던 중 3·1운동에 참여했다가, 일제의 수배를 피해 상하이를 거쳐 독일로 망명했습니다. 그곳에서 의학 및 생물학을 공부하는 한편 자전적 소설 ‘압록강은 흐른다’를 집필하는 등 한국의 문화와 정신을 독일 사회에 알렸습니다. 이미륵상은 이미륵 박사의 뜻을 기리고 한국과 독일의 문화 교류 및 상호 이해 증진에 기여한 인사에게 한독협회와 독한협회가 해를 바꿔가며 수여하는 상입니다.

items.title: 양재천의 만추
items.snippet: 걷는 걸 즐기게 되면 생활의 많은 게 달라진다. 같은 거리도 차를 타고 다닐 때는 보이지 않던 것들을 볼 수 있게 된다. 그래서 약속 장소가 그리 멀지 않고 시간적 여유가 있는 날에는 되도록 걸어간다. 먼 곳이라 차를 타고 가야 하는 경우에도 30분에서 한 시간 정도 일찍 도착해 주변을 구경하며 산책하듯 걷는다. 이런 여유가 일상에 자리 잡으면 길이 막혀 약속에 늦는 결례도 줄일 수 있다.

items.title: 한반도 밀고 들어온 중공군, 포로 75%는 왜 본국 귀환을 거부했나
items.snippet: 중국인민지원군(중공군)과 국군·유엔군의 최초 교전은 1950년 10월 25일 평안북도 운산에서 벌어졌지만, 중국공산당은 6·25전쟁 발발 1년 전부터 북한에 대규모 병력을 지원했다. 1949년 4월 마오쩌둥은 북로당이 요청한 중국인민해방군 소속 3개 한국인 사단의 북한 파병에 동의했다. 해방 이전 조선의용대는 중국공산당 팔로군과 연합해 항일무장투쟁을 전개했다. 해방 후 이들은 인민해방군 제4야전군에 배속돼 국공내전에서 장제스의 국민혁명군(국민당군)에 대항해 싸웠다. 이렇듯 실전 경험이 풍부한 정예 병사 최소 3만7000명이 1949년 7월부터 1950년 5월까지 북한으로 이동해 조선인민군(인민군)에 편입됐다. 6·25전쟁 개전 당시 남침 선봉에 섰던 인민군 21개 연대 중 10개 연대, 병사의 40% 내외가 이들 중국인민해방군 출신 한국인 병...

items.snippet: 국민의힘은 20일 민주유공자 예우에 관한 법률안(민주유공자법)이 범여권 주도로 국회 본회의를 통과한 데 대해 “이 법이 남길 것은 예우가 아니라 분열”이라고 비판했다. 국민의힘은 인정 기준이 모호해 공정성 논란을 피하기 어렵고, 이미 보상받은 이들에게 의료·양로·요양 지원을 더하는 것은 중복 혜택이라고 주장했다.국민의힘 박충권 수석대변인은 이날 논평에서 “법안은 희생과 공헌을 어떻게 구분할지, 사회적 공감대를 무엇으로 판단할지 구체적 기준이 전혀 보이지 않는다”며 “국민 세금으로 운동권 노후 무임승차를 위한 ‘운동권 특혜법’을 만들겠다는 민주당, 미래세대와 역사에 너무도 부끄러울 뿐”이라고 했다. 이어 “기준이 모호한 채로 시행되면 공정성 논란을 피하기 어렵다. 예우법인 만큼 지원과 혜택도 형평성을 살펴 과도하지 않도록 충분히 검토해야 한다”...

Long-term Madrid tenants living in former public housing allege Brookfield plans to let their rent-controlled leases expire and sell their apartments at unaffordable market prices.

items.title: Migrant caravan makes its way through Mexico to U.S. after Democrats win midterms
items.snippet: Emboldened by the results of this month's U.S. midterm elections, giving the Democrats control of Congress in the new year, hundreds of migrants are making their way from southern Mexico to the border with the United States — despite having almost no chance of gaining entry.

items.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear...

items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
items.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar exciton...

items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

items.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establ...

items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. items.title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have spin-orbit coupling among the strongest in semiconductors, yet whether their centrosymmetric bulk phases can convert charge current into spin current, and what controls the response, is unknown. Here we identify, from first-principles calculations on the four all-inorganic compounds CsBX3 (B = Pb, Sn; X = Br, I), the factors that govern their intrinsic spin Hall conductivity. The conductivity arises from the spin Berry curvature of the spin-orbit-split halide-p bands, 1.1-2.6 eV below the valence band maximum, and exceeds that of III-V and group-IV semiconductors when the Fermi level lies inside them. Because the valence band maximum is an s-p singlet, shifted only in second order, these contributions cancel in the undoped compounds, which respond like conventional semiconductors. items.title: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. items.title: Asymmetric Transistor Aging Under Thermal Gradients
items.abstract: Advanced technology nodes improve performance but increase susceptibility to BTI-induced aging. Using aging- aware circuit simulations, we show that realistic on-chip thermal gradients can cause significant asymmetric transistor degradation in 16 nm FinFET circuits, leading to setup and hold time violations. These results highlight the necessity of incorporating thermal-gradient-aware aging analysis into timing signoff to ensure chip reliability.

items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Atomic-scale assembly of sulfur vacancy complexes for tailored in-gap states in monolayer WS$_{2}$
items.abstract: Atomic-scale defects in two-dimensional semiconductors are quasi-isolated quantum systems with promise for emerging technologies. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. In this work we assemble sulfur vacancies in monolayer WS$_{2}$ into complexes of different sizes and geometries using the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states. items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.title: Delay Mismatches Shape the Spectra of Three Synchronized Semiconductor Lasers
items.abstract: We study a network of three synchronized chaotic lasers and the radio frequency spectra of the intensity fluctuations. The position and morphology of the peaks are significantly different depending on the set of lasers being synchronized. The lasers and coupling paths are similar but not identical in all parameters, including their feedback and coupling delay times. The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. items.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.title: A Probabilistic Behavioral RTL Simulation Framework for Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. items.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. items.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
items.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. items.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
items.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. items.title: From a High-T$\rm_C$ Spin-Gapless Semiconductor to a Spin-Glass: The Role of Disorder in NiMnCrAl
items.abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. items.title: Performance limits and benchmarking of ideal 2D topological insulator field-effect transistors
items.abstract: Topological insulator field-effect transistors (TIFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to overcome the scaling limits of silicon-based field-effect transistors (Si-based FETs). In this study, we establish the performance limits of ideal TIFETs and present a comprehensive benchmarking of the switching energy-delay performance of TIFETs against Si-based FETs (FinFET and LGAA) and 2-D material-based FETs ($\mathrm{MoS}_2$ and InSe) under equivalent and realistic conditions. items.title: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
items.abstract: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. items.abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. In this work, we show how localized electron excitation controls the generation of circularly polarized- and chiral cathodoluminescence from a single achiral plasmonic nanoantenna. items.title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic...

items.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
items.abstract: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random...

items.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
items.abstract: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody. We analyze a 3D box with such mirrors as walls to accumulate and store blackbody radiation. Applications include solar-powered thermal energy and solar-powered thermophotovoltaics. items.abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. items.abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. items.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
items.abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. items.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. items.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
items.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. items.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
items.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the ex...

items.title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
items.abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. items.title: DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration
items.abstract: Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not gu...

items.title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
items.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 μm. The continuous electroluminescent interface also reproduces complex contact patterns without computational rec...

items.title: Power Scaling Across Link Utilization with GPAM-4 Signaling and Event-Driven Reception
items.abstract: This work highlights the potential of combining event-based signaling with event-driven reception to achieve receiver power scaling across link utilization, without requiring wake-up, locking, or data-rate reconfiguration. The approach is demonstrated using the proposed four-level Gaussian pulse-amplitude modulation (GPAM-4) scheme and a corresponding event-driven receiver. By employing a resettable ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RRVCO) as its front end, the receiver achieves inherently event-driven symbol measurement, initiated directly by each received pulse. Symbols are decoded directly from the final RRVCO phase state, eliminating a counter-based back end. Simulated in 28-nm CMOS, the receiver power is evaluated across a $100\times$ range of effective data rates---from 0.15 mW at the peak rate of 8 Gb/s, down to 2.5 $μ$W under active/idle operation and 1.6 $μ$W under data rate c...

items.title: HDR-DTCP: High-Dynamic-Range Differential Tissue-Coupled Wireless Powering for Tunable Biphasic Stimulation in Injectable Implants

This work presents high-dynamic-range (HDR) differential tissue-coupled powering (DTCP), termed HDR-DTCP, a body-coupled architecture in which noninvasive differential electrodes establish an AC electric field in tissue and a thread-like implant extracts power from the longitudinal potential gradient for on-chip harvesting and stimulation. Distributed coupling along the implant length, rather than receiver cross-section, enables minimally invasive injectable geometries, with harvested power scaling with implant length. When tested on 1000 unseen variants of these seven designs, each corresponding to a different set of independently sampled transistor sizes, the accuracy is found to be within 5% of SPICE. items.title: On-demand valley control in a WSe2/CrPS4 heterostructure via optically programmed magnetic order

items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. items.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
items.abstract: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. items.abstract: Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors offer distinct advantages as imaging detectors for space-based X-ray observatories, being low-power, radiation-resistant, and operable at room temperature. Previous characterizations of the low-cost, commercially-available IMX290LLR-C back-illuminated CMOS sensor from Sony Semiconductor Solutions have found Fano-limited X-ray spectral resolutions while operated at room temperature and a radiation tolerance compatible with use in low Earth orbit. Here, we report the quantum efficiency of the IMX290LLR-C as measured across the soft X-ray band (200 - 1000 eV) using Beamline 6.3.2 of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. items.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
items.abstract: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. items.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
items.abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. items.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
items.abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. items.abstract: Edge AI increasingly relies on specialized accelerators for low-latency inference under tight resource and energy constraints, yet their efficiency remains limited by data movement. items.abstract: Machine learning in physical hardware promises to reduce training cost by colocating computation, memory and adaptation within device physics. items.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The novelty of the approach, called the Neural Physics method, is that it expresses the discretisation as a convolution neural network (CNN) whose weights are predetermined by the integrals of the basis functions in the FEM. The Neural Physics method is physically consistent as it represents a discretisation of the governing equation and can run on CPUs, GPUs and the latest AI accelerators, resulting in an increase in computational speed. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. The accuracy and speed of these methods is tested on a problem with a known analytical solution and compared to a standard FEM, and shows that the Neural Physics method is...

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: Adjoint-State Identifiability of Piezo-Tunable Valley Splitting in 2D Magnetic Heterostructures
items.abstract: Mechanical strain has been proposed to dynamically tune proximity-induced valley splitting in 2D magnetic heterostructures for solid-state information processing. While first-principles studies routinely predict strain-modulated valley splittings at the atomic scale, they rarely address whether the coupling parameter can be extracted from a macroscopic transport measurement against realistic device noise. This paper develops a classical, partial differential equation-constrained multiscale inverse framework to quantify the device-level identifiability of the exchange-strain coupling from a transverse Hall voltage in a molybdenum disulfide and chromium tribromide heterostructure. Structural relaxation confirms a chiral $C_3$ point-group symmetry of the Hollow-stacked structure, and Neumann's principle reduces the coupling tensor to a single scalar $η$. items.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
items.abstract: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. We present SyclKittens, a hardware...

items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These pri...

items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash cont...

items.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning
items.abstract: High-throughput calculations using density-functional theory (DFT) are commonly used to explore point defects for applications in power electronics and quantum technologies. There is currently a major shift away from these traditional simulation techniques towards machine learning (ML) methods. We explore a class of physics-guided ML models for predicting defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines (ZPL) to identify point defects for quantum applications. The models are specifically targeted for use in a prescreening step for accelerated high-throughput workflows, and are therefore designed to avoid the costly relaxation step typically present with ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We compare performance for single and double point defect systems in 4H-SiC with ridge, kernel ridge, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using three different descriptors representing the defect syste...

items.title: Thermoelectric properties of metal-semiconductor percolation composites
items.abstract: We analyze the thermoelectric response of composite materials comprising homogeneous semiconductor hosts with randomly distributed metallic inclusions. We demonstrate that the properties of such materials are strongly affected by the percolation transition (with background conductivity). We show that in the vicinity of the percolation threshold, the power factor and the thermoelectric figure of merit strongly depend on both the concentration and arrangement of inclusions. Finally, we identify promising regimes for enhancing the power factor in realistic composites.

However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale ima...

items.title: Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
items.abstract: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$π$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $π$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. items.title: OpenTherm: A Unified and Progressive Benchmark for 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient chip thermal prediction is essential for advanced packaging design. In recent years, deep learning-based thermal predictors have made significant progress, achieving high prediction accuracy while substantially reducing computational costs. However, differences in datasets, simulators, and evaluation protocols hinder direct comparison of existing methods and systematic assessment of their generalization across design variations and cross-package transfer scenarios. We introduce OpenTherm, an open benchmark combining 32,000 established 3D-IC samples with 50,000 new 2.5D chiplet samples generated with the open-source HotSpot simulator. It provides fixed data splits, a common input representation, and shared evaluation tools. items.title: Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
items.abstract: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local voltage into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances of a few k$Ω$ despite M$Ω$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. items.title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. items.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
items.abstract: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. items.title: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance.
